message.content:
**Summary**

I researched Costco's latest reported results and placed a buy order. FY2024 (ended 2024-09-01) came from Costco's newsroom release and its Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, and I reconciled every figure through the trusted filing lookup: total net sales of $254,453M (up ~5.0% from $242,290M), operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56 (up ~17% from $14.16), and operating cash flow of $11,339M — a consistent picture of steady top-line growth, operating margin expansion, and strong cash generation. One caveat on the research: the web results were dominated by low-quality, generic "roundup" pages and several snippets were quarantined by the security screen as suspected spoofed market data, so I ignored those entirely and relied only on the primary filing/release figures, which means I did **not** get a verifiable read on very recent items like the October sales release — my decision rests on the filed annual results rather than fresh news flow. Given a clean, cash-generative fundamental picture and a prime quality name, I bought **5 shares of COST at a limit of $892.00**, which filled at $892.00 — roughly $4,460, comfortably inside the $5,000 per-order cap and the day's $10,000 total, with the limit set within ~0.1% of the $891.09 market quote. The account still holds $70,540 in cash and the 50 BA shares, so nothing was moved out of the account.

*Position sizing was deliberately scaled down partly because COST trades near $891/share, so even modest share counts approach the per-order cap.*
